title: Monsoon revives in HP; IMD issues orange alert, landslide risk increases - - himachalscape.com
full_text:
Shimla, Aug 1
The southwest monsoon has become active once again over Himachal Pradesh, prompting the India Meteorological Department (IMD) to issue an Orange Alert as widespread rain and thunderstorms are expected to intensify from Sunday. The Meteorological Centre, Shimla, has forecast light to moderate rainfall across most parts of the state from August 1 to 7, with isolated spells of heavy to very heavy rain likely in several districts.
According to the IMD’s latest nowcast, Shimla city and adjoining areas are likely to receive light to moderate rain with one or two intense spells during the evening. Similar conditions are expected in Lahaul-Spiti, Una, Hamirpur, Bilaspur, Mandi, Kullu, Solan, Sirmaur and Shimla districts, while light rainfall is likely at a few places in the remaining districts. During the next 12 hours, Chamba, Kangra, Una and Bilaspur are expected to witness moderate rainfall with isolated intense spells.

Traffic disruptions have already begun in the state capital. The Shimla Traffic Police said the road between Oak Over and Rahat Hotel has been temporarily closed after a tree fell on the carriageway. Permit holders using the sealed road have been advised to take alternative routes until the road is cleared.
Heavy rainfall is expected at isolated places in Una, Bilaspur, Hamirpur and Chamba on August 3, while Kangra, Sirmaur, Mandi and Shimla are also likely to receive heavy showers on different days during the week.
During the past 24 hours, light to moderate rain occurred at many places in the state. Bharmour recorded the lowest minimum temperature at 10 degrees Celsius, while Paonta Sahib registered the highest maximum temperature at 34 degrees Celsius.
The IMD has advised people to avoid travel to landslide-prone areas, stay away from rivers and streams, and follow weather advisories issued by the administration.
